topic.title: The counteroffer
topic.claim: Your counteroffer is the raise you were never offered: the day you resign, the budget appears.
topic.moment: Asking for a raise twice and hearing 'next cycle', then a meeting with a number two days after resigning.

turn.believed: a counteroffer means the company values you
turn.actually: it's a correction: the price of keeping you, paid only when replacing you costs more

topic.because: as long as you stay quiet, the cheapest raise is none; a resignation changes the company's sum, not your worth
topic.payoff: The real appraisal is the day you resign.

cover.headline: Your counteroffer is the [raise you were never offered.]
cover.sub: The day you resign, the budget appears.

paragraphs: Your counteroffer is the raise you were never offered.
slides.why_swipe: it states the take; the reader wants to see how a resignation finds a budget

paragraphs: You asked twice this year. Both times: "budgets are tight, next cycle for sure."
Then you put in your papers. Within two days there's a meeting, and suddenly there's a number.
slides.why_swipe: the scene is familiar; why did the number appear only now?

paragraphs: I've watched this happen to friend after friend, and it always goes the same way.
Keeping you was never the question. The question was how little it would take. As long as you stayed quiet, the answer was nothing.
slides.why_swipe: the motive is out; what is a counteroffer, really?

paragraphs: **A counteroffer isn't a reward. It's a correction.**
It's the company admitting what you were worth, at the exact moment it became cheaper to pay you than to replace you.
slides.why_swipe: the turn has landed; who else knew?

paragraphs: Everyone in that meeting knows it. HR knows. Your manager knows. The only person hearing that number for the first time is you.
Part of you feels wanted. The other part wonders why it took a resignation letter.
slides.why_swipe: mixed feelings are out; where is the real appraisal?

paragraphs: So the real appraisal in an Indian office isn't in April.
**It's the day you resign.** Everything before that was a negotiation you didn't know you were in.

end.save: Read it again before your next appraisal meeting.
end.send: Send it to the friend who's been told "next cycle" twice.

draft.caption: Has a resignation ever got you the raise your appraisal didn't?
draft.alt_text: A text carousel arguing that a counteroffer is the raise you were never offered: companies find the budget only when replacing you would cost more.
